display: Coordinator of a migrant women's enterprise program at a Melbourne neighbourhood house (Box Hill, east Melbourne), supporting women who run catering, tailoring, hair and grocery businesses.

signals.text: I'm looking for a Mandarin-speaking person who understands accounts and can volunteer on a recurring basis in a small-business program for migrant women.
Our bookkeeping workshop is losing women who understand numbers well but not the English accounting terms. Three Chinese grocery owners dropped out in the first two weeks.
One interpreter for one hour doesn't work for us. We need the same person to sit next to a participant every week and explain BAS and invoices line by line in Mandarin.
We keep losing volunteers just as they become useful, to paid jobs and exams. I want a way to keep them for longer than a term.
I can't pay volunteers because the budget is fixed until June. I'm still looking for something other than money that makes people stay.
Next year's council funding review is in March. I need to turn this term's weak completion rates into a clear story with numbers and reasons.
I'm stretched thin with only a 0.4 FTE assistant, and I'd like to share the load with someone who can take on admin or workshop support.
I'm planning a wedding and negotiating the guest list between two families, which takes more energy than I expected.

offers.text: A free place in the neighbourhood house's Conversational English class for every volunteer, plus a reference letter after 40 volunteer hours.
A room for 20 people with a projector, a small kitchen and a children's corner, available for community workshops and meetings.
Three years of running workshops and one-on-one mentoring for migrant women starting small businesses, including how to design for people with limited English.
Introductions to the City of Whitehorse council, Moneycorp and a free legal advice service, for people who want to support or work with small migrant businesses.
A pool of about 30 volunteers, mostly retirees and university students, who can be matched to community projects.
Fluent English, Tamil and Hindi, with some conversational Mandarin. I can facilitate, translate and mentor in those languages.
A hands-on understanding of GST, BAS and invoicing in Xero as it applies to small shops, taught in an eight-week format.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a retired accountant who speaks Mandarin. I'd like to help small business owners in my community understand tax and bookkeeping, but I don't want to commit to a full-time role.
catchers.can: Match them with a specific participant for weekly sessions during the workshop. They would get a free English class if they want one, a reference letter after 40 hours, and a clear role.
catchers.confirm: Can you commit to sitting with the same person regularly (for example, one morning a week for the rest of the term)?

catchers.hypo: I'm a university accounting student who speaks Mandarin. I need volunteer hours and some real experience with small businesses.
catchers.can: Offer a recurring one-to-one support role in the bookkeeping workshop, with a reference letter after 40 hours and supervision from me.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to explain BAS, GST and invoices in Mandarin, not just translate general conversation?

catchers.hypo: I run a bookkeeping or tax business serving Chinese-speaking clients. I'd like to give back, and a bilingual glossary or short training for your participants is something I could do.
catchers.can: Use a bilingual glossary or a session in Mandarin to help women who understand numbers but not the English terms, and arrange a regular slot in the workshop.
catchers.confirm: Is this something you can offer in Mandarin repeatedly rather than as a single guest talk?

catchers.hypo: I work in community services and need evidence about outcomes and completion rates for a small migrant enterprise program ahead of a funding review. Can I trade ideas?
catchers.can: Share what I know about the program's data and trade ideas on turning weak completion rates into a story funders can act on.
catchers.confirm: Do you work with funders or councils on evaluating programs for migrant or small-business participants?

catchers.hypo: I'm a council officer interested in supporting migrant-owned shops in Whitehorse with small-business training that's accessible in languages other than English.
catchers.can: Introduce them to my contact at the City of Whitehorse council, who is supportive and focused on participation and completion numbers.
catchers.confirm: Does your work involve decisions about funding or supporting small-business programs for migrant communities in Melbourne's east?

catchers.hypo: I teach, and I know a few people who tutor English or run community classes. We'd like to find a program where our adult learners could practise English by helping out.
catchers.can: Through my fiancé, who is a teacher, introduce teachers or tutors who might refer adult learners as volunteers, with the free English class and reference letter as the benefit.
catchers.confirm: Do you have learners or students who would like volunteer hours and a reference letter in exchange for regular weekly support?

forbids.text: I can't pay volunteers. The program budget is fixed until June and I can only offer non-monetary benefits.
I won't share names or personal details of the women in the program.
I won't accept a one-off interpreter as a solution to the Mandarin gap, because the support has to be recurring and from one person.
I can't run a separate Mandarin-language class. There isn't budget or staff time for it.
I have very little spare staff time (0.4 FTE assistant only), so I can't take on projects that need heavy coordination from me.

projects.name: English Bookkeeping Workshop (Term 4)
projects.text: Eight-week workshop on invoices, GST, BAS and basic bookkeeping in Xero for women running small shops. Attendance has dropped because of English accounting terms, so we need recurring Mandarin-language support alongside participants.
roles_needed: Mandarin-speaking volunteer with bookkeeping or accounting knowledge

projects.name: Volunteer retention pathway
projects.text: Build a way to keep volunteers past the point they become useful: a free English class, a reference letter after 40 hours, and a clear role, without paying them.
roles_needed: Employer or organisation willing to recognise volunteer references

policy.t1: Workshop details, volunteer benefits and the specific gap I want filled (recurring Mandarin-speaking support who understands accounts), plus what the council needs from the program.
policy.t2: That I'm stretched thin and at risk of burnout, and that I'm planning a wedding. I'd share this only once there's trust and a clear collaborator.
policy.never: Names of participants and personal financial details.
